Ahead of UAlbany football’s first game, first year head coach Tom Perkovich says  the objective was to give his team an opportunity to win its season opener in the fourth quarter. The Great Danes did more than that by building a two-possession advantage heading into the final frame and holding on to win 28-14 over New Hampshire at Casey Stadium Friday night. “A lot of emotion obviously coming off the field after that win, right,” Perkovich said. “So many new faces, including our staff, players building on the guys that were here. Just really proud of everyone. Everyone involved in the organization.” It was a statement win for UAlbany as they kicked off the new year with a Coastal Athletic Association win. The Great Danes were in control pretty much the entire game by pounding the Wildcats' defense with 374 rushing yards on the evening. “It was definitely pretty awesome,” said Joey Koch, a junior running back who ran for a team-high 144 yards and one touchdown. “There’s been a lot of good running backs that have come through this place. Just waiting your turn, taking it day by day.” The start wasn’t ideal as senior Kai Colón, who got tapped just this week as the starting quarterback, threw an interception on UAlbany’s first drive of the game. New Hampshire turned it into a touchdown to take the lead 7-0 early. But Colon settled down by relying on his legs quite a bit as he rushed for 90 yards on 15 carries. He went 7-of-17 for 57 yards passing. “It means everything. I thought we played a great game,” Colon said. “A lot of stuff to work on, but a word I would have for this game is grit. I mean, we did what it takes- 1-0.” Junior Rahshan La Mons, who ran for 70 yards on 19 carries, tied the game at 7-7 with a one-yard touchdown run on the next drive. The Great Danes also got two rushing touchdowns from senior quarterback Aidan Semo, who had 28 yards on six carries in the game. UAlbany led 21-7 at halftime, and the two teams traded touchdowns in the third quarter to keep a 14-point game. Early in the fourth quarter, it appeared the Wildcats were primed to make it a one-score game as they were on the Great Danes’ five-yard line. But a tipped pass led to an interception by junior linebacker Dillon Dunathan, which ended New Hampshire’s scoring threat. “We want to play all three phases,” Perkovich said. “It might not be as sexy as some people want it, but the job’s to win games, right? And so we did that tonight. We controlled the clock, right. We put our opponent on their heels. In my opinion, we still have a ton to get better at.” Next up, the Great Danes travel to University at Buffalo for a Thursday night showdown against an FBS opponent. title: Huskies Secure 1st Win of 2026 with Decisive 5-0 Win Over UNH - University of Connecticut Athletics
content: MERION STATION, Pa. — No. 11 University of Connecticut (1-0) secured a decisive 5–0 victory over the University of New Hampshire (0-2) on Saturday at Ellen Ryan Field. UConn dominated with 26 shots, 20 of which were on goal, while maintaining a solid defensive front, allowing only one shot from New Hampshire. UConn started the first quarter with strong offensive pressure. Fien Hollander opened the scoring at 3:26, converting a penalty corner assisted by Milou Heuker and AJ Eyre. UConn continued to challenge the New Hampshire defense with shots from Olivia Machiavelli and Paige Keller, both saved by Kerigan Ross. The quarter concluded with UConn leading 1–0. UConn asserted control in the second quarter with a decisive performance. Early on, Lucy Zich capitalized on a penalty corner opportunity, scoring with assists from Milou Heuker and Charlotte Ritter at 15:48 to extend the lead. Later, Olivia Machiavelli increased the advantage by scoring her first goal of the season at 26:25, assisted by Paige Keller. UConn concluded the quarter ahead 3–0, maintaining a strong position heading into the next phase of play. UConn extended its lead early in the third quarter when Lucy Zich scored at 32:28, capitalizing on an intercepted pass in the circle. UConn continued to pressure New Hampshire's defense with multiple penalty corners and shots on goal, but Kerigan Ross made several saves to keep UConn from increasing its lead further. However, at 44:44, Abby Davidson converted a penalty stroke, marking her first goal of the season and securing a commanding advantage for the Huskies. The quarter ended with UConn ahead 5–0, which was the final score of the game. In the fourth quarter, UConn maintained its offensive pressure against New Hampshire, consistently pushing forward with multiple penalty corners and shots. Early in the quarter, UConn's Milou Heuker initiated three penalty corners between the 45:47 and 46:32 marks, leading to attempts by Marlijn Swaan and Lucy Zich, both of which were thwarted by New Hampshire's defense. Despite several attempts, including shots by Fien Hollander and Olivia Machiavelli, New Hampshire's goalkeeper, Kerigan Ross, kept the Huskies from increasing their lead with multiple saves. The quarter concluded without additional scoring, and UConn secured the victory with a final score of 5–0. Fien Hollander scored a crucial goal, which was also the game-winner. Lucy Zich tallied two goals and registered six shots on goal. Olivia Machiavelli found the back of the net with all three of her shots on target. Paige Keller contributed with an assist and recorded two shots on goal. UCONN Abby Davidson PENALTY STROKE GOAL, goal number 1 for season.

title: UNH Stock Gains Retail Attention: This UnitedHealth Move Could Make Getting Treatment Faster - Stocktwits
content: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) drew strong retail attention on Tuesday after announcing it will eliminate prior authorization requirements for 30% of healthcare services that previously needed insurer approval, a move that could ease administrative burdens and offer relief to doctors. UNH shares were down 0.3% in pre-market trading at the time of writing. UnitedHealth said the move is part of a broader push to make healthcare more accessible, affordable, and transparent, while easing administrative burdens across the system. Currently, prior authorization applies to only about 2% of the company’s medical services, and roughly 92% of requests are approved, typically within 24 hours. Within Medicare Advantage, a private insurance option, UnitedHealth maintains fewer authorization requirements than its peers. By the end of 2026, the company plans to eliminate another 30% of the remaining approvals, including some outpatient surgeries, diagnostic tests such as echocardiograms, and select therapies such as chiropractic care. The changes could bring relief to doctors, who have long criticized the paperwork-heavy process that can delay treatment, according to reports. UnitedHealthcare said it is investing in digital tools and artificial intelligence to streamline approvals, including features such as real-time tracking and faster decision-making. It has also proposed initiatives such as a gold card program to exempt certain providers from repeated approvals. Last month, UnitedHealthcare backed an industry push to standardize electronic prior authorization submissions, aiming to automate the process and make it easier for providers and patients. The company expects over 70% of its authorizations to follow this new system by year-end. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits turned ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ a day earlier. title: UnitedHealth Beats Q1 2026 and Raises Guidance - Is UNH Stock a Buy After Jumping 8%? - TradingKey
content: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) reported Q1 2026 results exceeding expectations with EPS of $7.23 and a Medical Care Ratio of 83.9%. The company raised its full-year EPS guidance to over $18.25 and generated $8.9 billion in operating cash. While technically showing overbought conditions, a decisive close above the $357 resistance level could target $380-$407. Valuation remains attractive at 18-19 times forward earnings. Potential risks include rising medical costs or contract losses impacting Optum Health. The Q2 MCR will be key to confirming the sustainability of Q1 improvements. TradingKey - UNH beat Q1 EPS by 10% at $7.23, MCR improved to 83.9%, and guidance raised to >$18.25. Stock jumped 8%. Key breakout level $357, targets $380–$407. Buy or wait? UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH) saw shares shoot up by 7 to 9% on April 21 after the Q1 2026 results came out and they were a whole lot better than people were expecting. The company's adjusted Earnings Per Share came in at $7.23 - that's 10% better than the average prediction and a major win considering where things had been. And a Medical Care Ratio of 83.9% was way under the 85% that most people were thinking it would be So it looks like UnitedHealth Group's Q1 2026 results might signal a big shift in the way they're doing things. Instead of trying to grow as fast as possible they're now focused on getting their margins back in shape. Yes, revenue came in at $111.7 billion which is a decent 2% gain, but the real star of the show was that Earnings Per Share figure. It crushed expectations by 10% - you don't see that kind of beat very often. And that was thanks in large part to a Medical Care Ratio of 83.9%. That's a big deal because it shows they're getting better at choosing which patients to insure and how much to charge them. To do that they had to get a bit ruthless about cutting any Medicare or Medicaid memberships that wouldn't bring in a healthy profit. Management seems pretty confident about the company's future, enough so that they've bumped up their full-year Earnings Per Share forecast. That suggests they think the things they're doing now - like being more selective about who they insure - are here to stay. Even though Optum Health is still dealing with some challenges they're now looking like contained problems rather than major roadblocks. With $8.9 billion in operating cash coming in they're feeling pretty good about handing some of that back to shareholders. They're sticking to their plan to buy back at least $2 billion worth of stock by the end of the next quarter. All that said, progress on their AI-driven claims processing system is also looking pretty promising. UNH has been on a tear ever since it broke out from its base at $255, and now its testing a very important zone between $345 & $357, where a bearish trendline and a 200 day moving average are converging. The fact that the stock popped through the earnings hurdle with good volume and demand was certainly a bullish sign, but with RSI close to 80, rest assured it's over bought now. To break through the downtrend, Unh just needs a decisive close above $357 - and if that happens, look out for the $380 & $407 targets to be in the cross hairs. Of course, if the price gets rejected at this resistance level, it'll likely pull back to $328 before we think about the next leg up. Traders need to keep a close eye on the charts for a high volume breakout above $357 - that'll be the cue to get long. If the price does get rejected at the resistance zone though, keep an eye out for a higher low in the $328-$335 range. That might be the better entry point. A stop loss below $328 is a good idea just in case the breakout fails. The argument for UNH being a buy at $350 is that it's got a strangle hold on the market and a valuation that's pretty appealing. It's trading at around 18-19 times earnings going forward, which is below its historical average of 22-24 times earnings. On top of that, you've got recovering margins, a 2027 Medicare Advantage rate hike that's already been confirmed and some serious cash on hand - $8.9 billion to be precise - to back it up. All of which adds up to a pretty solid case for buybacks and growth through AI. On the other hand, there's a bunch of reasons why UNH stock could be in for a tough time. If medical bills start to surge or if contract losses continue to be a problem for Optum Health, then the stock's got a lot of room for error. And things aren't made any easier by the fact that UNH is prioritising its profits over membership growth. That means top-line momentum is pretty limited, so investors are going to have to keep a close eye on the Q2 MCR - that'll really be the deciding factor as to whether Q1 was a one-off or the start of a trend. Well, it was a pretty strong set of numbers - the EPS was up by 8% and came in at $7.23, beating forecasts by about 10%. It was dominated by a pretty impressive medical care ratio of 83.9% and a raised forecast for the full year of $18.25. And then there was the $8.9 billion cash flow - that was a big deal, because it showed that UNH was past the worst of its margin worries from 2025. UNH has raised its adjusted EPS floor to $18.25 and it's still guiding for revenue to come in above $439 billion. That's because of some smart pricing and efficiencies through AI, plus the confirmed 2027 Medicare Advantage rate hike. If the stock can break through the $357 mark and stay there, then it could easily push on through to $380 and even $407. Fundamentally, UNH is still trading at a pretty attractive 18-19 times earnings - that's below its historical average. But it's worth keeping in mind that if UNH can't keep up the good work on medical care ratios, then that whole story could change. title: UNH football opens season with 28-14 loss at UAlbany - Seacoastonline.com
content: ALBANY, N.Y. — Senior quarterback Brooks Bentley threw for 230 yards and two touchdowns, but the University of New Hampshire football team fell to UAlbany, 28-14, on Friday at Bob Ford Field at Tom and Mary Casey Stadium. Senior wide receiver Ja’Carree Kelly led the Wildcats’ receiving corps with six catches for 123 yards, including a 45-yard touchdown reception. Myles Thomason paced the ground game with 53 rushing yards and also caught a 4-yard touchdown pass. Defensively, sophomore linebacker Trevor Barry recorded a career-high 13 tackles, while sophomore safety Cohen Cook added 10 stops. Darren Burton II also came up with an interception for UNH. · On the first possession of the game, Burton II intercepted Colón’s pass at the UAlbany 45 to give the ball to the Wildcats. ·UNH, on the opening drive, took advantage of an Albany personal foul on a 37-yard field goal attempt that extended the drive. Bentley lofted a pass to the left flat corralled by Thomason at the 8-yard line and he ran into the end zone at 8:07 for the first score of the season. Lucas Glassburn kicked the PAT to give the ‘Cats a 7-0 lead. Trailing 21-7, it took UNH only two plays to cover 74 yards in 37 seconds to trim the deficit at 14:21 of the third quarter. Thomason ran around the left end for a 29-yard gain to the UAlbany 45, then Bentley connected with Kelly in stride down the middle of the field for a 45-yard touchdown. The Wildcats return to action on Saturday, Sept. 5, when they travel to face Syracuse.

title: GO-NORTH Programs Give Youth a Summer of Healthcare Career Exploration - University of New Hampshire
content: UNH's efforts to strengthen the region's healthcare workforce were in full force this summer, with youth career exploration programs across the state giving students hands-on introductions to healthcare careers. Thanks to funding from the Governor’s Office of New Opportunities and Rural Transformational Health (GO-NORTH), 147 students participated, at no cost, in summer healthcare career exploration programs hosted by organizations across the state. GO-NORTH was established by executive order under Governor Kelly Ayotte and is funded through the federal Rural Health Transformation Program. GO-NORTH advances five strategic initiatives to improve the health and long-term sustainability of rural New Hampshire, including a Workforce Initiative focused on building and retaining a skilled rural healthcare workforce through education, training, and career pathways. This summer, GO-NORTH funding supported youth engagement programs to introduce students to healthcare and allied health professions while creating pathways that could help strengthen New Hampshire's future healthcare workforce. Students at the Southern New Hampshire Area Health Education Center Camp in Manchester learned about careers firefighting. Southern New Hampshire Area Health Education Center (SNHAHEC) Health Career Exploration Camps: Held throughout July, the camps included a Seacoast program at UNH July 13-17, a Nashua camp July 20-24, and a Manchester camp July 27-31 in partnership with UNH Manchester. The camps gave middle and high school students a hands-on look at a wide range of healthcare careers. Through simulations and interactions with healthcare professionals, students explored careers in nursing, emergency medicine, public health, physical therapy, behavioral health, dentistry, and emergency preparedness. All three camps also included CPR certification. Riverside Rest Home Future Healthcare Professionals Summer Exploration Program: This program gave high school students an 80-hour summer experience centered on career exploration within a long-term care facility. Participants rotated through areas including nursing, rehabilitation, dietary services, and activities while taking part in structured shadowing and reflection. St. Joseph Hospital Health Careers Academy: This five-day, hospital-based summer program gave students a chance to explore multiple healthcare careers. Students shadowed healthcare professionals, took part in simulations and toured different departments, learning about both clinical and non-clinical roles, including emergency medical services and trauma care. The program also introduced students to some of the challenges of delivering healthcare in rural communities and showed them potential next steps, including LNA training, scholarships and nursing education programs. Southern New Hampshire Health's Beyond the Stethoscope: This six-week, full-day summer program gave high school seniors an opportunity to explore the many roles that make a healthcare system run. Through simulations, department rotations, career panels and individualized coaching, students learned about clinical, technical, administrative and allied health careers while exploring potential paths to college, training and employment. Students practice CPR at the St. Joseph Hospital Health Careers Academy. Other RHT-supported programs included the Rockingham County Healthcare Academy in Brentwood; MWV School to Career Health Camp at Memorial Hospital in North Conway; and Colby-Sawyer College's Fueling Interest in Health & Allied Health Careers program in New London. While the programs varied in length and focus, they shared a goal of building students' interest in healthcare by giving them immersive, hands-on experiences and opportunities to see where that interest could take them. "We were excited for the opportunity to support nine unique youth health care career exploration programs hosted by seven different organizations across New Hampshire," says Ken La Valley, executive director for Rural Health Education." Providing hands-on experiences that allow New Hampshire youth to explore health care careers in a fun and engaging way aligns directly with our goal of creating pathways to strengthen the state's health care workforce." These projects are supported by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) as part of a financial assistance award totaling $204,016,550.20 with 100 percent funded by CMS/HHS. title: UNH poll shows Ayotte leads Warmington in NH governor’s race - WCAX
content:
DURHAM, N.H. (WCAX) - A new poll sheds light on the race for New Hampshire governor. Republican Governor Kelly Ayotte is up against presumptive Democratic challenger Cinde Warmington, who is expected to win the Democratic primary on Sept. 8. New data from the UNH Survey Center shows that among the 2,100 people polled, Ayotte leads Warmington 49% to 39%. Nine percent remain undecided. Ayotte’s approval rating is just about split down the middle. Data show 49% of respondents approve of her performance as governor and 42% disapprove. Eighty-six percent of Republicans and 53% of Independents approve of Ayotte’s performance, while only 11% of Democrats approve. title: Huskies Kick Off 2026 Season with Matchups Against UNH and #20 Saint Joseph's - University of Connecticut Athletics
content: STORRS, Conn. – The UConn women's field hockey team kicks off the 2026 season with a matchup against the University of New Hampshire followed by a match against no.20 Saint Joseph's. The Huskies will open the season against New Hampshire on Saturday August 29 at noon and will face off against Saint Joseph's Sunday August 30 at 2pm on ESPN+. The Huskies will begin the 2026 season with plenty of new faces. Despite the new roster, UConn enters the season ranked no.11 in the NFHCA preseason poll and will have an abundance of experience on the pitch. UConn returns Natalie McKenna in goal with Fien Hollander, Olivia Donahue and Milou Huecker anchoring the back line, while Olivia McKenna leads the midfield. UConn will look towards its sophomore class to take a leap as, Abby Davidson, Emma Larit, Keet Castelijn, Sydney Moritz, and Addy Infante will all look to contribute on field. Alongside their incoming freshman, the Huskies hit the transfer portal adding athletes with BIG10 experience from the University of Maryland. The Huskies added Maya Everett, Faith Everett, AJ Eyre, and Ellie Goldstein from Maryland and brought in Marlijn Swaan from the University of New Hampshire. This is the third consecutive year the Huskies have opened the season with matchups against the University of New Hampshire and Saint Joseph's. Last season the Huskies took down New Hampshire by a final score of 4-3 to open the season before falling to no.9 Saint Joseph's by a final of 2-1 in a shootout. The Huskies match against Saint Joseph's will be streamed live on ESPN+.
